deep.reconstruction:
The page is a pure table with no derivation. It is sheet (11) of a multi-sheet table; sheets (10) and (12) continue it with other column ranges. Columns are the primes q = 367, 373, ..., 503. Rows are the primes p = 191, 193, ..., 433, grouped in blocks of seven by heavy rules. A small circle at (row p, column q) marks that q is a quadratic residue mod p, i.e. Legendre symbol (q/p) = +1. A blank cell means q is a nonresidue. Circles in orthogonally adjacent cells are joined by short strokes, which produces the chains and squares. These strokes appear to be only a visual aid for reading the pattern; they carry no extra arithmetic content that I can detect.

Verification of the reading (my computations):

Row p = 191. Reduce q mod 191 and apply reciprocity.
- 383 ≡ 1, 397 ≡ 15, 409 ≡ 27, 421 ≡ 39, 431 ≡ 49, 433 ≡ 51 and 449 ≡ 67 are all residues. All of them carry circles.
- 367 ≡ 176, 373 ≡ 182, 379 ≡ 188, 389 ≡ 7, 401 ≡ 19, 419 ≡ 37, 439 ≡ 57 and 443 ≡ 61 are all nonresidues. All of them are blank.

The decisive test of orientation is the pair 191, 383, where both primes are ≡ 3 mod 4.
- (383/191) = +1 and (191/383) = −1.
- The cell is marked, so the column number is tested against the row modulus.
- The pair (191, 379) agrees: (379/191) = −1, cell blank.

Row p = 251, all 24 columns. The residues among the column primes are exactly {373, 431, 443, 449, 491, 503}. Those are precisely the six circles drawn in that row.

Spot check (397, 367): (367/397) = (30/367) = +1, and the cell is marked.

In the lower blocks the diagonal cells (p, p) for p = 367, 373, 379, 383, 389 also appear to carry circles. This suggests Gauss counted q ≡ 0 as marked, or used the circle as a filler on the diagonal; the image is not fully conclusive.

Purpose: an extensive empirical table of the quadratic character of primes with respect to primes. It is of the kind underlying Gauss's empirical discovery and induction of the reciprocity law (Disq. Arith. art. 95ff., which has a much smaller table of residues for moduli up to 97). The table as a whole implicitly displays the reciprocity relation between (q/p) and (p/q) for the pairs present on both sheets.
errors: No arithmetic errors found in the cells I checked (all of row 191 from 367 to 449, all of row 251, and the cell (397, 367)).

Possible inconsistency: diagonal cells (p,p) appear to be marked in some rows, although p is not a quadratic residue of itself in the Legendre sense. This is a convention issue, not an error, and needs confirmation on the original.

results.what: Table of Legendre symbols (q/p) for primes q from 367 to 503 (columns) and primes p from 191 to 433 (rows); a circle marks a quadratic residue.
results.modern_name: Table of quadratic residues / Legendre symbol table (quadratic character of primes)
results.usually_credited_to: Such tables were computed by Gauss (Disquisitiones 1801, table II) and later by Jacobi (Canon arithmeticus, 1839) and others.

results.what: Graphical device of joining adjacent residue marks horizontally and vertically into chains and squares.
results.modern_name: Visual pattern display of a quadratic-character matrix (no standard name)

deep.surprise_reason: It is well known that Gauss computed large tables of quadratic residues and discovered quadratic reciprocity empirically. This sheet is a part of such a table. The connecting-line visualization is a curiosity but not a new result.

checkable.asserts: Row 251 of the table: exactly these column primes are quadratic residues mod 251, matching the six circles.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.ntheory import legendre_symbol; all(legendre_symbol(q,191)==1 for q in [383,397,409,421,431,433,449]) and all(legendre_symbol(q,191)==-1 for q in [367,373,379,389,401,419,439,443])
checkable.asserts: Row 191: marked cells are residues, blank cells are nonresidues, for columns 367 through 449.
Orientation test: the circle at (191,383) means column-prime residue mod row-prime, not the converse.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.ntheory import legendre_symbol; legendre_symbol(367,397)==1 and legendre_symbol(367,359)==1
checkable.asserts: Cells (397,367) and (359,367) are marked as residues.

transcription_corrections: The machine description is correct in outline. The specific meaning is: a circle at (row p, column q) iff q is a quadratic residue mod p.
The top-right annotation read as '4061' is uncertain; it may be a later archival foliation or shelf mark. The circled '(6)' is the folio number.
The red crayon '11' in the middle of the sheet is the sheet number of the table series (cf. '10' and '12' on the adjacent sheets), matching the '(11)' at top left.
The faint pencil header near columns 383–397 reads 'Math. 1' (archival shelf mark).
